additional_info.subject: ID0468113-DC/Si-D/DE-[Y2 / T0 4002926227] Power aperage issue CRM:03056000802
additional_info.body:
Dear Miriam,
Thank you for contacting eMobility Support.
After carefully checking the logs of the timestamp being given, we find that the OCPP went offline during the charging session.
When the OCPP connection goes offline, the charger can`t provide any requests to the backend of the charger, and this is the reason there was a voltage drop.
The OCPP connection can go offline, because of an unstable network connection with the network provider, or because the router had trouble finding a signal.
Right now i see that the OCPP connection is stable and no errors are showing.
I will keep an eye on the charger for the next three days, to see if the problem occurs again.
Please provide me with feedback if this answered your question, or if you are still facing issues.
Thank you.
Kind regards,
Priscilla van Wettum
eMobility Support

additional_info.subject: ID0468113-DC/Si-D/DE-[Y2 / T0 4002926227] Power aperage issue CRM:03056000802
additional_info.body:
Hello Miriam,
Thank you for your quick response.
Hereby a visual to see that the charger is working properly and charging at the moment:
It should be an error in your own backend system indeed.
Regarding you second question. Please check the following steps:
Define the MeterValuesAlignedData List
Purpose: Once you've set the interval, the system needs to know what specific measurements (measurands) should be collected and reported at each ClockAlignedDataInterval within a MeterValues.req PDU.
Implementation: You'll need to provide a comma-separated list of these measurands. This list tells the system which data points to capture at the specified clock-aligned times.
Related Parameter: Be mindful of MeterValuesAlignedDataMaxLength, which defines the maximum number of elements that can be included in this list. Your implementation should respect this limit.
Define the StopTxnAlignedData List
Purpose: Similar to MeterValuesAlignedData, this parameter specifies which clock-aligned periodic measurands should be included in the TransactionData element of a StopTransaction.req PDU for every ClockAlignedDataInterval of the transaction.
Implementation: This also requires a comma-separated list of measurands, but specifically for the StopTransaction context.
Related Parameter: StopTxnAlignedDataMaxLength dictates the maximum number of elements allowed in this list, which your implementation must adhere to.
Please let us know if we can help you with something else, or if you are still facing issues.
Thank you.
Kind regards,
Priscilla van Wettum

additional_info.subject: ID0468113-DC/Si-D/DE-[Y2 / T0 4002926227] Power aperage issue CRM:03056000802
additional_info.body:
Hello Miriam,
Thanks for the feedback.
What I see from your logs/configs:
Non-Working Charger:
It shows a single meter reading (value: "10615406.548562588") at a specific timestamp (2025-12-29T08:00:00.016Z).
Crucially, this request is missing a transactionId. It only specifies connectorId: "0". This means the meter value is not explicitly linked to an ongoing charging session.
Working Charger Log:
It also shows a single meter reading (value: "97830833") at a specific timestamp (2025-12-24T06:45:00.073Z).
This request explicitly includes cp:transactionID and cp:connectorID. This is a key difference!
Why this matters:
When a charger sends
MeterValues
during an active charging process, it typically includes the
transactionId
to link those readings to that specific session. The
ClockAlignedDataInterval
setting is to ensure these in-transaction, periodic meter values are sent.
If the non-working charger sends
MeterValues
without a
transactionId
, your backend might interpret them as general periodic readings for the connector (or even ignore them for session tracking), rather than as intermediate readings for an ongoing charge. This would explain why you only see a "final reading at the end" or why intermediate readings aren't being processed or displayed correctly for the 18-minute session.
Also the configuration looks the same, so I don't believe the configuration to be the problem.
As you can see below, our charger sent the MeterValues at your 9:00 am and you send us an acknowledgement.
Of course, since the session was very brief, there is no more logs to check but in any case, every 15mins we are sending for all connectors.
Is it possible that the logic for the non-working charger that it's catching the connector ID = 0 instead of ID = 2? And since the backend doesn't care too much about connector ID 0, it doesn't process the data properly?
I will wait for your feedback
Best regards,
Francisco
